title: POC Weekly Sync - Throughput Optimization
next_steps: Redwood to share latest benchmark sheet with 99th pct latency and concurrency curves
Customer to run 1-hour stress test with 200 concurrent sessions and share logs
Schedule deep-dive on queueing & admission control next Tuesday
AE to send pricing variant for Dedicated pools with burst tier
action_items: Diego - update batching config recommendations for conversational workload (due: 2027-11-15)
Tom - enable detailed p99 tracing in staging and send logs (due: 2027-11-12)
Maya - send benchmark spreadsheet + notes from today's call (due: 2027-11-11)
Sara - validate tokenization variance across sample prompts and share set (due: 2027-11-14)
summary: Quick sync to review throughput numbers after applying continuous batching and concurrency caps. Redwood and Novapay align on tuning: increase max concurrency to 150, tune admission control/queueing to reduce tail latency, and run longer stress tests. Agreed next steps include benchmark share, 1-hour stress test, and follow-up deep-dive on queueing policies.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, can see a couple folks joining now
[00:08] Sara Patel: hey sorry i'm a few minutes late, site had an incident, i'm here now
[00:12] Diego Alvarez: no worries Sara, we'll recap quickly, we ran the new cont-batch profile overnight
[00:18] Tom Nguyen: quick heads up we also flipped on p99 tracing in staging at 1am, saw some interesting outliers
[00:25] Liam O'Connor: the product asks were mostly about whether the higher concurrency would tank tail latency, that's what i'm most curious about
[00:32] Maya Chen: perfect, agenda: numbers, where we see regressions, config suggestions, next steps. Diego do you want to kick off with the throughput slides?
[00:40] Diego Alvarez: yeah, um so rough summary, after enabling continuous batching with a target batch size of 48, average throughput increased ~1.6x for our short-turn prompts, tokens per second improved but we did see p99 jump in a couple windows, i think due to admission control saturation
[00:58] Sara Patel: sorry can you repeat the batch target, 48?
[01:02] Diego Alvarez: yeah, target 48, with dynamic windowing so smaller requests get packed as well, but when concurrent sessions hit above 120 we saw queues pile up
[01:12] Tom Nguyen: those queues were visible as request_wait in our traces, some requests waited up to 320 ms before entering the kernel scheduler
[01:21] Diego Alvarez: exact, and that waiting pushed some p99 above our agreed SLO. but p50 and p95 improved across the board
[01:28] Sara Patel: our goal is consistent sub-200ms p95 for the majority of calls, p99 ideally under 500ms, is that still realistic with the batching profile?
[01:36] Diego Alvarez: yes, with a couple changes — add an upper concurrency cap of 150 and enable an aggressive admission control policy: preferentially serve low-latency routes, plus a small fairness window to avoid starvation
[01:47] Maya Chen: to clarify, cap at 150 concurrent requests across the Dedicated pool or per instance?
[01:52] Diego Alvarez: across the pool in this POC because you're on a 4-node Dedicated pool, that gives us room to distribute batches. we can also scope per-instance limits if you want tighter bounds
[02:01] Priya Rao: how does that interact with burst capacity? we might want short bursts for peak checkout traffic
[02:06] Diego Alvarez: bursts are supported via the burst tier, but the admission control will still apply; bursts help throughput but without queueing limits you'll risk tail latency spikes. suggestion: keep bursts for 30-second windows with a token bucket and higher priority for checkout routes
[02:20] Sara Patel: hmm, okay. can you show the concrete numbers from the spreadsheet?
[02:24] Diego Alvarez: sure, i'll share the live sheet after. quick numbers from last run: with cont-batch + target48 and no concurrency cap: avg throughput 1,200 rps, p95 170ms, p99 610ms. with cap=150: avg throughput 1,050 rps, p95 180ms, p99 420ms
[02:44] Liam O'Connor: so we lose about 12% throughput but p99 drops a lot; that's a tradeoff we can accept for checkout flows
[02:51] Sara Patel: checkout is our high-sensitivity route, yes. for background processing we can accept higher tails
[02:56] Tom Nguyen: another thing — we saw some tokenization variance for long form prompts which created bigger batches and longer kernel runs, those correlate with the worst p99s
[03:07] Diego Alvarez: good point — you can normalize token counts by truncating or using a preflight tokenizer check client-side, or we can configure a max batch kernel size to split big ones
[03:18] Sara Patel: is that a Redwood config or something we have to change on our side?
[03:22] Diego Alvarez: configurable on Redwood side: batching policy includes max_kernel_size and per-request metadata hints, but it's helpful if you also surface expected token length per route
[03:31] Maya Chen: i also wanted to call out KV cache behavior — when you have many short-turns sharing a context, the KV hits improve, which helps throughput. but when context sizes vary it can increase memory pressure and slow scheduling
[03:44] Priya Rao: memory pressure is something we saw in staging. do you recommend lowering the cache ttl?
[03:49] Diego Alvarez: yes, for the pilot set a 2-minute TTL for session KV cache and enable prefix cache, that gives you benefits without long-lived memory retention
[03:58] Sara Patel: ok noted. another question — what about queue admission priorities, can we set checkout as high priority and background as low?
[04:04] Diego Alvarez: absolutely, Redwood supports route-level priority and token buckets per route. you can map routes -> priority classes in the Console, or through the API if you want infra-as-code
[04:15] Tom Nguyen: can we see a sample config?
[04:17] Diego Alvarez: i'll paste a snippet after, it's in the doc i sent last week, might have been called batch-tuning-v3, i'll resend
[04:24] Liam O'Connor: question about metrics — how do we attribute cost per route when batching mixes different routes in one kernel run? we need per-route chargebacks
[04:33] Maya Chen: good question. Redwood Console reports token-level usage and attributes tokens to original route ids based on request metadata, then cost is apportioned. it's not perfect but it's close enough for billing and optimizations
[04:45] Sara Patel: ok we need that to validate the cost impact of increasing batch sizes
[04:50] Diego Alvarez: from our benchmarks, moving from batch 24 -> 48 reduced token compute cost per request by ~18% in many cases, but depends on prompt length distribution
[04:59] Priya Rao: and quantization? we heard that 4-bit quantization might change latency patterns
[05:03] Diego Alvarez: quantization lowers memory footprint and can increase throughput, but kernel latency sometimes increases slightly for some ops; we can recommend a quant eval matrix for your model family
[05:12] Sara Patel: we'll want that matrix. can Redwood run a quant eval against our sample prompts?
[05:16] Diego Alvarez: yes, we can. propose we do small sweep in staging during the 1-hour stress test
[05:21] Maya Chen: let's talk about the 1-hr stress test: Tom, can you run 200 concurrent sessions with token length distribution A and B that Sara shared?
[05:29] Tom Nguyen: yes we can. we'll schedule this tonight and send logs. do you want p99/p95/gc traces included?
[05:34] Diego Alvarez: please include p99, p95, kernel scheduler wait times, and request_wait histograms, that'll help us pinpoint the admission spikes
[05:42] Liam O'Connor: one more ask — what's the recommended concurrency target for the Dedicated pool size we have?
[05:47] Diego Alvarez: for your 4-node gpus and observed prompt distribution, 100-150 concurrent is the sweet spot. 100 favors lower tails and slightly lower throughput, 150 gives more throughput but you need admission rules to keep p99 bounded
[05:59] Sara Patel: say we pick 150 — what alerts should we set?
[06:02] Priya Rao: yes alerting specifics are helpful
[06:04] Diego Alvarez: set alerts on p99 > 500ms sustained for 30s, request_wait > 200ms for more than 5% of requests in a minute, and kernel_queue_length > threshold (i'll send thresholds). also alert on node memory > 80%
[06:18] Maya Chen: i'm going to summarize so we're aligned: 1) Redwood shares updated benchmark sheet and batch-tuning snippet; 2) Novapay runs 1-hour stress test with 200 concurrent and shares logs; 3) Diego updates recommended config (cap=150, admission policy, prefix cache TTL=2m); 4) follow-up deep-dive on queueing next Tue. correct?
[06:36] Sara Patel: correct, and we'll also evaluate quantization sweep during the stress test
[06:40] Tom Nguyen: i'll run the stress tonight and email logs; expect them in the morning PST
[06:44] Diego Alvarez: i'll prep the config changes and the benchmark sheet, sending by EOD tomorrow
[06:49] Maya Chen: perfect, thanks everyone. any other questions?
[06:52] Speaker 6: nope all good from my side
[06:55] Maya Chen: ok wrap up, we'll follow up on action items, thanks all
[06:58] [call ends]
